bugs.rootCause: React Native on Android never draws a skew. In RN 0.86, BaseViewManager.setTransformProperty runs the transform through TransformHelper.processTransform, then MatrixMathHelper.decomposeMatrix, and passes the View only translation, rotation (rounded to 3 places), scaleX/Y and camera distance. The decomposition does compute a skew (ctx.skew), but nothing applies it, because android.view.View has no skew setter. Reanimated's transform takes the same path. So the skewX(-8deg) on the gold face and edge (tactile.tsx, Button.tsx) came out as a plain rectangle. Jest passed because it only checked the style objects.
bugs.fix: New apps/mobile/src/components/ui/slant.tsx. slantTransforms(deg) splits skewX into a closed-form 2x2 SVD: an outer view that rotates about -42.99° and stretches (scaleX 1.0727, scaleY 0.9322), and an inner view that rotates about 47.01°. outer·inner is exactly skewX(-8°) about the centre, and each part is something an Android View can apply, so the same code draws on both platforms. Slant renders the two views as an absolutely placed, pointerEvents-none sibling behind the content. In TactileSurface with skew, the edge is a Slant (edge colour, radius, depth offsets) and the face's whole look (faceStyle: gradient, inset highlight and shade, border, disabled flat look) moves onto a slanted plate inside the face box. The face box keeps the layout, the press translateY and an explicit NO_BORDER, and the label sits upright beside the plate. Button.tsx: the label counter-skew (UNSKEW) is gone. Non-skewed surfaces are unchanged. No SVG or Skia: Skia must stay off the startup path (startupGraph), and native styles keep the gradient and the NO_BORDER guard as they were.
bugs.test: apps/mobile/src/components/ui/__tests__/slant.test.tsx (new): outer·inner equals skewX for -8/8/-20/0°. rep.notes:
Root cause confirmed in node_modules/react-native 0.86.3 (ReactAndroid uimanager). BaseViewManager.setTransformProperty runs TransformHelper.processTransform, then MatrixMathHelper.decomposeMatrix, then sets only setTranslationX/Y, setRotation/X/Y, setScaleX/Y and setCameraDistance. decomposeMatrix computes ctx.skew, but nothing reads it. TransformHelper applies skewX to the matrix (m[4] = tan), and the decomposition then discards it.

Decision (mine, per rule 7): no react-native-svg or Skia shape. Instead, an exact SVD split of the shear into rotate·stretch·rotate on two nested Views (slant.tsx). Why:
- Skia must stay off the startup path (startupGraph.test).
- An SVG path needs onLayout measuring, which risks a first-frame flash, and it would re-implement the gradient, the inset lines and the border.
- Native views keep the existing faceStyle recipe and the NO_BORDER guard as they were.
- Cost: 2 extra plain views per slanted face, 1 per edge.
- iOS and Android share one code path and one look.

The rotation rounding Android applies (3 places) costs less than 0.001 dp; this is covered by a test that replicates the Android pipeline.

Test ID convention for slanted surfaces:
- `${testID}-face` stays the face box (layout and press).
- The look moved to `${testID}-face-shape`.
- The edge box is `${testID}-shadow` or `${testID}-edge`, with its look on `-shadow-shape` / `-edge-shape`.
- Non-slanted surfaces are unchanged.

QA catalog steps that read the face colour of a primary by resource-id should use the new -shape ids.

Behaviour changes:
- Labels and 'VS' are now never counter-skewed, so upright on both platforms. FoundView's 'VS' used to be skewed on iOS.
- A slanted slate, danger or disabled button's content box is 1 dp wider on each side, because the border lives on the plate now.

Not changed (out of scope):
- TokenArt.tsx's Warp wobble (arsenal icon animation) still uses skewX. Android shows only its swell. It is listed with this reason in the source-scan test's ALLOWED map.
- warpModel.ts's existing note about Android skew is untouched.

Other notes:
- Button.test.tsx and ModesAndGameType.test.tsx were already CRLF in the working tree before this workflow. The edits kept CRLF. `prettier --check` flags those two files for line endings only; content diff is empty.
- docs/design/components.md: §0.7 item 4, §1.1 anatomy and Container row, and §3.5 updated (targeted edits).
- Nothing needed adb or an APK.

issues.problem: The device check for 'צור חדר' expects the wrong number. The rows y≈2040 and y≈2150 are 110 px apart, so a −8° slant moves x by tan 8° × 110 ≈ 15.5 px at any density, not 'about 17-18 px'. 17-18 px is the lean over the button's whole height. A QA tester who measures exactly as written may wrongly mark a correct build as failed.
issues.evidence: tan(8°) = 0.1405, and 0.1405 × 110 px = 15.46 px. The original B16 report expected 'about 18 px' between the top and the bottom of the button, which is a different measurement.
issues.suggestion: In the QA step, either measure at the face's top and bottom rows (about 17-18 px for a 48 dp button) or accept about 15-16 px between y≈2040 and y≈2150.

It stacks 'משחק חדש' and 'צפייה חוזרת' vertically, but the secondary keeps `skew`. components.md §1.0 and §1.2 say a secondary is 'Not skewed on its own': it slants only beside the primary in one row. This skew now really draws on Android, so at large text the stacked secondary shows as a lone slanted slate.

issues.problem: The 'on Android' component tests (tactile.test.tsx, and slant.test.tsx 'on Android too') swap Platform.OS. Slant and TactileSurface have no platform branch, so these tests pass the same on any platform and add no Android-specific coverage. The real proof is slant.test.tsx's replica of RN's compose/decompose/drop-skew pipeline, which does fail on the old code.
issues.evidence: slant.tsx and tactile.tsx contain no `Platform` reference. I checked the replica (`matrixOf` CSS order, `androidDraws` rotation = -atan2(row1[0], row0[0]), the determinant flip, the 3-place rounding, T·R·S draw order) against node_modules/react-native 0.86.3: TransformHelper.processTransform runs multiplyInto(result, result, helper), which gives result = helper·result in row-vector form. MatrixMathHelper.decomposeMatrix matches the replica, and BaseViewManager.setTransformProperty sets only translation, rotation, scale and camera distance.
issues.suggestion: Optional: rename or comment these tests so nobody reads them as Android rendering tests. The replica test is what guards the fix.

rev.summary:
I found nothing of medium or high severity. The skew fix is correct and complete.

**Root cause.** I confirmed it in node_modules/react-native 0.86.3 (ReactAndroid uimanager). BaseViewManager.setTransformProperty (lines 573-635) runs TransformHelper.processTransform, then MatrixMathHelper.decomposeMatrix, then sets only setTranslationX/Y, setRotation/X/Y, setScaleX/Y and setCameraDistance. The computed ctx.skew is never applied. So skewX on a view is dropped on Android.

**The fix (apps/mobile/src/components/ui/slant.tsx).**
- It is the closed-form SVD of [[1,k],[0,1]]: sx = √(1+k²/4)+|k|/2 and sy = √(1+k²/4)−|k|/2. The outer view rotates by (a2+a1)/2 ≈ −42.99° and then stretches. The inner view rotates by (a2−a1)/2 ≈ 47.01°.
- I checked this against RN's real pipeline:
  - multiplyInto applies the transforms in CSS order, so outer = R·D.
  - decomposeMatrix returns exactly that rotation and scale with zero skew. Android draws it as T·R·S, rotating about the view's centre.
  - Both views fill the same box, so they turn about the same centre.
  - ReactViewGroup sets clipChildren=false, so the rotated inner view is not clipped.
- The composite is an exact skewX about the centre on both Android and iOS.
- The edge is sheared about its own centre, so it is exactly the face moved straight down.

**TactileSurface, Button and the VS badges.**
- The face box keeps the layout, the press translateY and an explicit NO_BORDER. Its look goes onto the plate through faceStyle, which sets a border width in every state, so the disabled → gold NaN-border crash guard still holds and stays pinned by the faceStyle border-width test.
- The label is upright with no counter-skew. The hit area and accessibility are unchanged (the Slant views are pointerEvents none and not accessible).
- Reduced motion is untouched, and no UI strings changed.
- ConfirmModal, Modes footer, Results, friends room 'התחל משחק' (primary), join 'הצטרף' (primary), VsBadge (DuelHud, ScoreLine) and FoundView all render through the Slant.
- Apart from the Slant code itself, the only skewX left in app code is TokenArt's wobble, which is allowed with a stated reason.

**By-design claims.** 'שתף קישור' and 'העתק קוד' are not in the start button's row (one is in the scroll content, the other in the footer), which matches §1.0/§1.2. The disabled primary staying slanted matches §0.7.

**Clipping check.** I found no overflow:hidden ancestor near any slanted button that would clip the corners that stick out.

**Tests and checks I ran.**
- `npx jest` on slant, tactile, Button, ConfirmModal, ModesAndGameType, resultsDesign, components/player and screens/match: 378/378 green. ModesAndGameType failed once on a first run while another agent was editing, then passed 65/65.
- The wider run over ui, home, account, results and the solo/botPracticeEnd e2e: 931/932. The one failure is homeTransitions' profile-card (another area).
- levels, friends and leaderboard: the only failures are 'useRetiredStacks is not defined' in AvatarArt.tsx, which another agent is mid-edit on.
- `npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit`: one error, in i18n compose.test.ts (another area).
- eslint --max-warnings 0 on all 11 changed or created code files: clean.
- The new tests would fail on the old code: the -shape ids, the SLANT transforms, the source scan, and the Android pipeline replica, where a plain skewX gives a straight box.
- The fixer's change list touches none of the peer-session files.

**Low notes.** The B16 device check's 17-18 px figure should be about 15.5 px for rows 110 px apart. Results' new stacked layout (another area) keeps the secondary slanted when it is alone. The Platform.OS-swapped tests add no Android-specific coverage.

final.notes:
Root cause confirmed in node_modules/react-native 0.86.3 (ReactAndroid uimanager). BaseViewManager.setTransformProperty runs TransformHelper.processTransform, then MatrixMathHelper.decomposeMatrix, then sets only setTranslationX/Y, setRotation/X/Y, setScaleX/Y and setCameraDistance. decomposeMatrix computes ctx.skew, but nothing reads it. TransformHelper applies skewX to the matrix (m[4] = tan), and the decomposition then discards it.

Decision (mine, per rule 7): no react-native-svg or Skia shape. Instead, an exact SVD split of the shear into rotate·stretch·rotate on two nested Views (slant.tsx). Why:
- Skia must stay off the startup path (startupGraph.test).
- An SVG path needs onLayout measuring, which risks a first-frame flash, and it would re-implement the gradient, the inset lines and the border.
- Native views keep the existing faceStyle recipe and the NO_BORDER guard as they were.
- Cost: 2 extra plain views per slanted face, 1 per edge.
- iOS and Android share one code path and one look.

The rotation rounding Android applies (3 places) costs less than 0.001 dp; this is covered by a test that replicates the Android pipeline.

Test ID convention for slanted surfaces:
- `${testID}-face` stays the face box (layout and press).
- The look moved to `${testID}-face-shape`.
- The edge box is `${testID}-shadow` or `${testID}-edge`, with its look on `-shadow-shape` / `-edge-shape`.
- Non-slanted surfaces are unchanged.

QA catalog steps that read the face colour of a primary by resource-id should use the new -shape ids.

Behaviour changes:
- Labels and 'VS' are now never counter-skewed, so upright on both platforms. FoundView's 'VS' used to be skewed on iOS.
- A slanted slate, danger or disabled button's content box is 1 dp wider on each side, because the border lives on the plate now.

Not changed (out of scope):
- TokenArt.tsx's Warp wobble (arsenal icon animation) still uses skewX. Android shows only its swell. It is listed with this reason in the source-scan test's ALLOWED map.
- warpModel.ts's existing note about Android skew is untouched.

Other notes:
- Button.test.tsx and ModesAndGameType.test.tsx were already CRLF in the working tree before this workflow. The edits kept CRLF. `prettier --check` flags those two files for line endings only; content diff is empty.
- docs/design/components.md: §0.7 item 4, §1.1 anatomy and Container row, and §3.5 updated (targeted edits).
- Nothing needed adb or an APK.

bugs.rootCause: Three causes. (1) Server: matchmaking started the countdown the instant the last player connected (D37), often within a few hundred ms of 'found'. The count message then arrived while the phone was still busy entering the room and mounting the VS, so the '3' was already partly gone when the countdown view rendered. (2) Client: matchModel.countdownStep showed ceil((goAt−now)/1000). A count first shown late (slow message, busy phone, clock-sync error in hostGoAt) skipped straight to '2' or '1'. Nothing guaranteed each digit gets shown. (3) MatchScreen called onPlay the moment the snapshot arrived. When the board came at or before the phone's own GO, GO! was mounted and replaced in the same frame, so it never became visible (motion.md `go`: the board 400 ms after GO).
bugs.fix: Server (authoritative): see B43. The count now starts at least FOUND_HOLD_MS (1200) after 'found', when the phones are idle. Client: matchModel.countdownStepOver(remaining, span). Under 250 ms per digit the first digits are dropped. countdownStep(remaining) is unchanged for its other callers. MatchScreen also records when GO! first showed and calls onPlay only after GO_HOLD_MS (= tokens sequence.matchFound.boardRevealAt − goAt = 400), on the screen's own useNow tick. rep.notes:
Decisions made on my own:
(1) VS minimum time is enforced on the server. It is FOUND_HOLD_MS = 1200 after 'found', taken from tokens sequence.matchFound.countdownAt and DS-Motion '+1.2s'. It is a protocol constant plus the MatchmakingConfig.foundHoldMs config, so Moshe can lengthen it. FoundView pops the 'מוכן' badges 800 ms after the VS mounts, so with 1200 ms they are on screen about 0.4 s. If Moshe wants the ready reaction to linger, raise FOUND_HOLD_MS.
(2) The client handles the remaining lateness and clock-sync error without moving GO: a late count runs its 3 digits evenly over the time left, never skipping one. GO stays on server time, so the board still comes for everyone at once.
(3) GO! is held 400 ms before the board (motion.md `go`), checked on MatchScreen's 100 ms useNow tick. I first wrote the hold with setTimeout. That made 8 tests in __tests__/ranked.e2e.test.tsx crash in Reanimated's jest frame-callback mock (a router.replace from inside a fake timer). The tick-driven version passes them all and is simpler.
(4) The friends lobby's start and 'יציאה מהחדר' are now a pinned footer, the same pattern as GameTypeScreen, so the start button is also always visible. The design doc lines were updated.
(5) Join: a status line in the button's place, matching the Friends-Join mock. The shared Button is untouched.

Server change: apps/server/src/matchmaking/service.ts and packages/protocol need a staging deploy before B43 (and the server half of B37) can be checked on the phones. Without the deploy, B37's client half (pacing and GO hold) works on its own.

Known residual (not fixed, to keep the server change minimal): if the app is killed mid-game in a friends room and reopened, the rejoin gets a snapshot but no lobby, so the opponent's avatar falls back to the silhouette for that session. An in-app 'נסה שוב' keeps the avatars, because retryOnline passes the profiles on. Fixing the kill case needs FriendsRoom to send the lobby to a player who comes back after the start.

Not touched: GameScreen comments that still say profiles come from 'a ranked match'. The GAME agent owns that file.

Housekeeping: I created and deleted a temporary debug test copy (apps/mobile/src/__tests__/zzOnlineAgentDebug.e2e.test.tsx) while tracing the e2e crash. It is gone. Other agents' concurrent edits seen in FoundView.tsx, docs/01-SPEC.md and components.md were left intact. My doc edits were small targeted insertions.

issues.problem: When the board arrives before the phone's own GO, the new 400 ms GO! hold shows GO! with no GO sound or haptic. In that case the model jumps straight from 'countdown' to 'play', so `beat` becomes 'play' and never 'countdown-go'.
issues.evidence: MatchScreen.tsx:112 `const beat = model.kind === 'countdown' ? `countdown-${model.step}` : model.kind;` and :118 `else if (beat === 'countdown-go') cue('go');`. The new test 'the board before the phone's own GO: GO! still shows, and holds' checks the text and onPlay but not the cues. Before the fix, GO! was never visible in this case, so the missing cue went unnoticed.
issues.suggestion: Treat the 'play' beat like 'countdown-go' when the previous beat was a digit, for example map `model.kind === 'play'` to 'countdown-go' in the beat. Then assert cue('go') in that test.

issues.problem: Known gap, which the fixer reported. If the app is killed during a friends-room game and rejoins, the host gets a snapshot but no `lobby`. `profiles` is then null and the opponent is a grey silhouette again: in the card, the locked cell, reactions and results.
issues.evidence: onlineSession.ts:242-247: the getter reads only `this.host.online.lobby`. FriendsRoom (apps/server/src/rooms/FriendsRoom.ts) calls sendLobby only in the lobby phase (lobbyChanged/onJoin while gamePhase === 'lobby'), and super.onJoin after the start sends no lobby.
issues.suggestion: Follow-up: have FriendsRoom send its last `lobby` (or the seats' avatarId and country) to a player who rejoins after the start. Or carry the avatars in the snapshot's player info. Add a rejoin test.

issues.problem: Clock skew is handled only one way. If the phone's goAt is LATER than the real GO (host clock sync error), 'started'/hasGame forces 'go' and cuts '1' short, or skips it when the skew is over 1 s. A late count is now compressed, but this case is not. Also, the screen-reader label still says '3 seconds' while a compressed count has less time left.
issues.evidence: matchModel.ts:232 spanMs = goAt − countdownSince. The 'started' phase forces remainingMs = 0 (line ~231), and MatchScreen shows GO as soon as model.kind === 'play'. CountdownView.tsx:50 builds the label from `m.step`, not from remainingMs. In practice the error is small: the matchmaking-message estimate (now + startsAt − serverTime) uses the same latency as 'started'.
issues.suggestion: Acceptable as is. Optionally, when 'started' arrives with digits still pending, pace the remaining digits over a short floor before GO, or just note the limit in motion.md. Optionally use remainingMs for the a11y label.

issues.problem: Comments still describe profiles as a ranked match's only. Friends rooms now fill them from the lobby. Affected: GameScreen.tsx:215 and :465, DuelHud.tsx:38, ConnectionLayer.tsx:40, OpponentLeft.tsx:35, resultsModel.ts:310/495, and OnlineSessionDeps.profiles (onlineSession.ts:137).
issues.evidence: e.g. GameScreen.tsx:465 "from the session's profiles (a ranked match)". resultsModel.ts:310 "(a ranked match's profiles)".
issues.suggestion: Update the wording to 'a ranked match's found, or a friends room's lobby'. The GAME agent owns GameScreen.tsx, so leave that file to it.

rev.summary:
I found nothing of medium or high severity. All 7 items are fixed at their root causes, and every relevant suite I ran passes.

B42/B51 (opponent shows as a grey silhouette in friends rooms): OnlineSession.profiles is now a getter. Ranked games still use the profiles from "found"; friends rooms read avatarId and country from the lobby seats. I confirmed:
- RemoteGameHost never clears `lobby`, and FriendsRoom sends no lobby after the start, so the cached object stays stable. The game screen's useMemo is safe.
- GameScreen's avatar map feeds the card, the locked-cell head, the reactions and the arsenal. The results screen gets the live OnlineSession instance, not a spread copy, so the getter works there too.
- The ranked-only loading card still needs names, so friends rooms don't show it.

B37/B43 (VS screen and countdown):
- Server: everyoneIn() keeps the server authoritative. The hold timer is cleared in clearMatchTimer, which fail() and close() both call. A player who drops during the hold is waited for, and readyCheck still bounds the wait.
- Client: countdownStepOver gives exactly the old countdownStep for a full count; I checked every remaining time from 1 to 3000 ms. countdownSince and goSince use the same systemClock as the matchmaking client. The 400 ms GO hold runs on the useNow tick, which stays enabled in the 'started' phase.
- The "ready" smile and nod is driven by seat.ready when the 'ready' message arrives, not by the 800 ms badge pop. So most of the 900 ms nod fits inside the 1.2 s hold.

B40/B53 (exit button under the Android navigation bar): there is now a pinned footer with the bottom inset added to its padding. Sharing the enter style between two views is supported in Reanimated 4.5.1.

Join ("מצטרף לחדר…"): a status line takes the button's place, as in the Friends-Join design. It reuses an existing key, present in all 19 locales. No hard-coded strings.

The new tests would fail on the old code (null profiles, an immediate countdown, a count shown late showing '2', no footer or joining testIDs).

- Jest, 16 suites / 281 passed: friendsHost, GameScreenOnline, screens/match, screens/friends, and the server's service and stealth matchmaking tests.
- Jest, more suites, all passing: server integration (matchmaking, ranked.e2e, appMatchmaking.contract, stealth.e2e, fourPlayers.e2e, stealthWiring.contract), mobile ranked.e2e, gameStoreOnline, onlineSession, packages/protocol, ModesRanked, roomLinks.e2e, resultsModel, gameRoute.

Only low items remain:

- The disclosed gap: an app killed mid-game in a friends room and rejoined shows the silhouette again.

bugs.rootCause: Three causes. (1) Server: matchmaking started the countdown the instant the last player connected (D37), often within a few hundred ms of 'found'. The count message then arrived while the phone was still busy entering the room and mounting the VS, so the '3' was already partly gone when the countdown view rendered. (2) Client: matchModel.countdownStep showed ceil((goAt−now)/1000). A count first shown late (slow message, busy phone, clock-sync error in hostGoAt) skipped straight to '2' or '1'. Nothing guaranteed each digit gets shown. (3) MatchScreen called onPlay the moment the snapshot arrived. When the board came at or before the phone's own GO, GO! was mounted and replaced in the same frame, so it never became visible (motion.md `go`: the board 400 ms after GO).
bugs.fix: Server (authoritative): see B43. The count now starts at least FOUND_HOLD_MS (1200) after 'found', when the phones are idle. Client: matchModel.countdownStepOver(remaining, span). Under 250 ms per digit the first digits are dropped. countdownStep(remaining) is unchanged for its other callers. MatchScreen also records when GO! first showed and calls onPlay only after GO_HOLD_MS (= tokens sequence.matchFound.boardRevealAt − goAt = 400), on the screen's own useNow tick. The friends room countdown is unchanged. Docs: 01-SPEC §10 (ספירה לאחור), motion.md §4.6 rows countdown.digit and go.

final.notes:
Decisions made on my own:
(1) VS minimum time is enforced on the server. It is FOUND_HOLD_MS = 1200 after 'found', taken from tokens sequence.matchFound.countdownAt and DS-Motion '+1.2s'. It is a protocol constant plus the MatchmakingConfig.foundHoldMs config, so Moshe can lengthen it. FoundView pops the 'מוכן' badges 800 ms after the VS mounts, so with 1200 ms they are on screen about 0.4 s. If Moshe wants the ready reaction to linger, raise FOUND_HOLD_MS.
(2) The client handles the remaining lateness and clock-sync error without moving GO: a late count runs its 3 digits evenly over the time left, never skipping one. GO stays on server time, so the board still comes for everyone at once.
(3) GO! is held 400 ms before the board (motion.md `go`), checked on MatchScreen's 100 ms useNow tick. I first wrote the hold with setTimeout. That made 8 tests in __tests__/ranked.e2e.test.tsx crash in Reanimated's jest frame-callback mock (a router.replace from inside a fake timer). The tick-driven version passes them all and is simpler.
(4) The friends lobby's start and 'יציאה מהחדר' are now a pinned footer, the same pattern as GameTypeScreen, so the start button is also always visible. The design doc lines were updated.
(5) Join: a status line in the button's place, matching the Friends-Join mock. The shared Button is untouched.

Server change: apps/server/src/matchmaking/service.ts and packages/protocol need a staging deploy before B43 (and the server half of B37) can be checked on the phones. Without the deploy, B37's client half (pacing and GO hold) works on its own.

Known residual (not fixed, to keep the server change minimal): if the app is killed mid-game in a friends room and reopened, the rejoin gets a snapshot but no lobby, so the opponent's avatar falls back to the silhouette for that session. An in-app 'נסה שוב' keeps the avatars, because retryOnline passes the profiles on. Fixing the kill case needs FriendsRoom to send the lobby to a player who comes back after the start.

Not touched: GameScreen comments that still say profiles come from 'a ranked match'. The GAME agent owns that file.

Housekeeping: I created and deleted a temporary debug test copy (apps/mobile/src/__tests__/zzOnlineAgentDebug.e2e.test.tsx) while tracing the e2e crash. It is gone. Other agents' concurrent edits seen in FoundView.tsx, docs/01-SPEC.md and components.md were left intact. My doc edits were small targeted insertions.

bugs.fix: (1) A CountChips component: the chips are a wrapping row, 4 columns while every label fits in up to 2 lines broken between words. Each label reports its lines via onTextLayout. A new exported pure helper breaksInsideWord(text, lines) detects a mid-word break, ignoring CJK/Thai, spaces and hyphen/ZWSP hints, and so does a 3+ line label. Either one steps the columns down to 2×2, then 1 a line. The step happens once per layout (stale reports are ignored, the grid remounts per column count) and resets on a new window size, font scale or language. Labels no longer have numberOfLines, so never '…'. (2) The header Text and the award title Text lost numberOfLines and wrap at word boundaries. issues.problem: The B20 fix probably does not fix the bug. Removing flexWrap from the parent changes where whole flex items go. It does not change how text breaks inside a single Text. The move Text ('A2 → 4', about 64 dp) and the technique fit easily on one line of a card about 300 dp wide. So Yoga still gives the move Text exactly its measured width, the same 181 px box as before. Android's StaticLayout then lays out 'A2 → 4' in that box. If the drawn width is wider than the measured width, it still breaks before the '4' and hides it on a second line the box can't show. The new `move: { flexShrink: 0 }` does nothing, because 0 is already React Native's default. The fixer's own report says the native cause is 'inferred, not proven on a device'. The results screen's bestRow drawing the move whole can be explained by position: there the move is the second child, so in RTL its edges round to the pixel grid differently. It is not evidence that the wrap flag was the cause.
issues.evidence: Diff: `moveRow: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'baseline', gap: space[5] }` (flexWrap removed), plus `move: { flexShrink: 0 }` and `technique: { flexShrink: 1 }` (ReplayParts.tsx ~line 449). The bug report's bounds [814,1159][995,1213]: 181 px wide and 54 px tall, about 19 dp at 2.8125, so the box is one line tall and exactly as wide as the text, with the '4' on a hidden second line. The new test ('the move line is never wrapped or narrowed… (B20)') only checks style props (parent has no flexWrap, move flexShrink 0, technique numberOfLines 2). It passes whether or not Android can still break the line, so it doesn't pin the behaviour on the device.
issues.suggestion: Make the move line impossible to break, whatever width it gets. For example, numberOfLines={1} with ellipsizeMode="clip" on the move Text, plus a 1–2 dp end padding as a buffer. Or draw cell, arrow and digit as three Text nodes in a row, the way Replay.dc.html uses three spans in a nowrap flex row. Then check on the A16 in Hebrew at normal and largest font: 'A2 → 4' with the digit visible. Keep the test, but make it assert the no-break mechanism, for example numberOfLines 1 or separate nodes.

bugs.rootCause: Confirmed in React Native 0.86.3's Android sources. The move was one Text, ltr('A2 → 4') = '⁦A2 → 4⁩', in a row, so Yoga gave it exactly its measured width (181 px). TextLayoutManager.measureText builds a StaticLayout with the builder's default text direction, FIRSTSTRONG_LTR. TextLayoutManager.kt:1058 even has 'TODO: Handle text direction (see View#getTextDirectionHeuristic)'. The ReactTextView (a TextView) then lays the text out again at draw time with its own heuristic, FIRSTSTRONG_RTL in an RTL app. The isolate hides every strong letter from first-strong detection, so the text was measured as an LTR paragraph and drawn as an RTL one. The screenshot shows the draw side is RTL: the line 'A2 →' is right-aligned (ALIGN_NORMAL) inside its 181 px box. The draw-time layout needed slightly more than the measured width, broke at the last space, and pushed the '4' onto a second line that the one-line box (54 px, lineHeight 19 dp) does not show. The reviewer is right that the earlier fix could not help: flexWrap on the parent does not affect line breaking inside a Text, and flexShrink 0 is already the default. numberOfLines 1 would not help either: on Android, ReactTextView.setNumberOfLines only calls setMaxLines, so the TextView still breaks the line and hides or ellipsizes the rest.
bugs.fix: New component components/player/MoveText.tsx draws the move as Replay.dc.html does, as three spans in an LTR row that never wraps: each word of the translated move ('A2', '→', '4') is its own Text, side by side, with direction 'ltr', alignItems baseline, and the design's gap of 4. A Text with no space and no isolate has no break opportunity: 'A2' starts with a Latin letter, so measure and draw both read it LTR (a BoringLayout on both sides), and '→' and the digit are single characters. ReplayParts uses it for the explanation card's move. The card's accessibility label still says the whole '⁦A2 → 4⁩'. The no-op `move: { flexShrink: 0 }` style was removed. The technique keeps flexShrink 1 and numberOfLines 2 beside it. The results screen's move of the game drew the same single ltr() Text in a row (the same latent bug, seen whole there only by sub-pixel luck), so it uses MoveText too (testID results-best-move). MoveText is exported from components/player.

final.notes:
Review issues addressed:
(1) MEDIUM, B20: the reviewer was right that removing flexWrap could not fix it. I traced the real mechanism in node_modules/react-native 0.86.3. TextLayoutManager measures with a StaticLayout that uses the default FIRSTSTRONG_LTR (there is an explicit TODO at TextLayoutManager.kt:1058). ReactTextView then draws through TextView with FIRSTSTRONG_RTL in an RTL app. The LRI…PDI isolate hides every letter from first-strong detection, so measure and draw used different paragraph directions. The screenshot shows the draw side is RTL: 'A2 →' is right-aligned in its box. numberOfLines 1 with ellipsizeMode clip would NOT fix it on Android, because ReactTextView.setNumberOfLines only calls setMaxLines, so the TextView still breaks the line and drops or ellipsizes the '4'. So I took the reviewer's second option: MoveText draws cell, arrow and digit as separate Texts in an LTR row, matching Replay.dc.html's three nowrap spans. None of them has a break opportunity. I applied it to the results' move of the game too, because the same single-Text pattern there is the same latent bug. The levels best-move line is a Hebrew sentence in a full-width column, so it is not at risk, and I did not touch it.
(2) LOW, QA catalog: updated the 4 lines with Edit (no reformatting); catalog.test.ts passes. That is why serverChanged is true. It is QA catalog data only, no server code, and it takes effect with the next staging deploy.
(3) LOW, 'אני' in ranked replays: documented in docs/01-SPEC.md §13.1 as an override of Replay.dc.html, which shows my name, together with the friends-room subtitle (B44). Worth mentioning to Moshe as a visible change in ranked replays.
(4) LOW, ja/ar/tr/id/vi 'match' word in solo practice: kept, on purpose. docs/i18n/glossary.csv defines 'game' as 対戦 / مباراة / maç / pertandingan / trận đấu ('One game played on a board'). docs/i18n/style/ja.md:56 says '対戦 is one game; ゲーム is the app or the game in general', so ゲーム would break the style guide. The app already uses 対戦 in strings shown in solo practice, e.g. the D65 freeze '対戦を凍結中'. Per-mode keys stay possible if Moshe wants them.
(5) LOW, stale docs: DECISIONS-PENDING §3.7 'built now' is rewritten for B1. The withDecimal comment in format.ts no longer mentions the score line; withDecimal is still used by howToPlayFixtures.

Decisions:
(1) B7: I added a generic opt-in ScreenHeader `wrapTitle` in the shared file apps/mobile/src/screens/home/parts.tsx instead of shortening translations, so the 19 names stay consistent with the Modes row. Only the map uses it; every other header keeps the one-line title. The B3/B8 agents can reuse it for the 'משחק חדש' title. The size steps are driven by onTextLayout, because Android's adjustsFontSizeToFit cannot see mid-word breaks. A long title can therefore take 1-3 extra frames to settle when the map opens.
(2) B27: I used a leading RLM in the he/ar translations rather than FSI-isolating names in code. It works on every platform and version without depending on isolate-aware first-strong detection, and it covers both visible lines and labels. A new test enforces the rule for the levels namespace. The Edit tool wrote the RLMs as literal invisible characters, not ‏ escapes; account.json deleteGoogleBody already does the same. The updated test files also contain literal RLM characters, the same way the repo's tests already use literal LRI/PDI.
(3) B39: besides the gate case, I also handled stage 300 ('תקבל 0 כוכבים.') and the quitCountsAsPlayed=false config. The text follows the same computation as the result's 'לשלב הבא', so the dialog and the result can no longer disagree.

rev.summary:
בדקתי את חמשת התיקונים באזור מפת השלבים, וכולם מטפלים בסיבת השורש. לא מצאתי בעיה בחומרה בינונית או גבוהה. מצאתי ארבע הערות קלות.

**לפי באג:**

- **B33:** אומת מול node_modules/@react-native/virtualized-lists/Lists/VirtualizedList.js:1616-1660. ‏‎_onContentSizeChange‎ קורא ל־‎_maybeScrollToInitialScrollIndex‎ (רק כש־initialScrollIndex>0, כלומר מפרק 2 והלאה, כמו שלב 17) ואחר כך ל־props.onContentSizeChange. לכן place() אחרי שני האירועים בא תמיד אחרון. הבדיקה החדשה (it.each לשני הסדרים) נכשלת על הקוד הישן בסדר layout→content. הרשימה משתמשת ב־getItemLayout, והפאנל לא מכסה את הרשימה, לכן 40% מגובה הרשימה נמצא מעל הפאנל.
- **B7:** הפתרון הוא opt-in ‏wrapTitle שמשתמש רק במפה, עם צעדי גודל לפי onTextLayout. המדידה מראה שכל 19 השפות נכנסות בגודל 18 ליד "900/900". ההערות הקלות: הכותרת בעברית תעבור לשתי שורות בגודל 28 מ־100 כוכבים, בניגוד לבדיקת המכשיר שבדוח. גם יש התנגשות קלה עם המיקום של B33, מרווח של 3.6dp בלבד לגרמנית, ושבירת מילה בגודל טקסט מערכת גדול.
- **B30:** המתקן לא שינה קוד. הוא מסתמך על שינוי botRoom של סוכן מקביל ב־Avatar.tsx, ווידאתי שהשינוי קיים בעץ. צילום ה־QA מאשר את האבחנה: תג עגול של כ־22dp שבו "בוט" נשבר ל"בו", כ־7dp בתוך שולי המסך ולא חורג מהם.

- **B39:** ‏afterQuit משתמש באותו nextAfterAttempt וב־withAttempt (quit, 0 כוכבים) שבהם משתמשת התוצאה ב־play.tsx:449. החיבור נעשה בשלושת המסלולים: levelChrome דרך play.tsx, ‏TapLevelScreen ו־PuzzleLevelScreen, וה־hooks נקראים בלי תנאי. המפתחות החדשים קיימים ב־19 השפות עם תרגום סביר.

bugs.rootCause: LevelMapScreen scrolled the map to the 40% spot from FlatList's onLayout. FlatList (VirtualizedList._maybeScrollToInitialScrollIndex) jumps to initialScrollIndex, which is the top of the chapter, the first time its content is laid out. On the phone the content layout came after the list's layout, so that jump overrode the placement. The map showed the chapter's gateway and stages 11-13, and stage 17 with my token stayed hidden under the docked panel.
bugs.fix: LevelPath now passes FlatList's onContentSizeChange up as onContentReady. LevelMapScreen places the map once, after both the list height and the first content layout are known, whichever comes second. VirtualizedList calls our onContentSizeChange only after its own initial jump, so our openOffset scroll always comes last. follow() and onJump are unchanged.
bugs.test: LevelMapScreen.test.tsx: new it.each 'B33: the list's own jump to the chapter's top never undoes the 40 % placement'. It covers both orders (layout then content, content then layout). It spies VirtualizedList.prototype.scrollToIndex and FlatList.prototype.scrollToOffset, and checks there is exactly one placement to openOffset(17), made after the jump. The existing 40 % test now fires contentSizeChange too.

bugs.rootCause: The map header (ScreenHeader) draws the title on one line (numberOfLines=1, screenTitle 28) beside the 'star N/900' chip. Measured with Rubik's real advance widths, the room on a 360 dp phone is about 151 dp with the widest chip. The titles need 221-349 dp in es, pt-BR, de, fr, ru, it, tr, id, pl, vi, th and nl. German 'Etappentraining' is a single 230 dp word, so wrapping alone would break it in the middle of the word. Android's adjustsFontSizeToFit does not detect a mid-word break.
bugs.fix: ScreenHeader gets an opt-in wrapTitle prop, used only by LevelMapScreen. The title (WrappingTitle) starts at screenTitle size with no line limit. It reads the phone's own lines (onTextLayout), and while they are more than 2 lines, cut short, or broken inside a word (wrapsWhole), it steps down 2 at a time to TITLE_WRAP.minSize 18, with the line height scaled. At 18 it allows 2 lines with an ellipsis as the last resort. A new title starts again at full size. CJK and Thai titles have no spaces, so they get one line. The default ScreenHeader path is unchanged. components.md §19.3 is updated.

It covers: wrapsWhole cases (break at a space with or without the trailing space, mid-word, 3 lines, cut short); the step-down via textLayout events, line height, the minimum and the 2-line limit, and the reset on a new title; and, in all 19 languages plus en-XA, that the map title fits whole on at most 2 lines at size 18 beside 'star 900/900' at 360 dp (measured with the shipped font). Hebrew fits at full size. LevelMapScreen.test also asserts that the header uses the wrapping title.

On the 22 dp 'cell' avatar of the panel's bot row, the chip was at most 22 dp wide, so 'בוט' wrapped and only 'בו' showed (the zoomed screenshot shows a 22 dp round chip with the ט wrapped below). The chip is 7 dp inside the screen, so the screen edge was not the cause.

final.notes:
Decisions:
(1) B7: I added a generic opt-in ScreenHeader `wrapTitle` in the shared file apps/mobile/src/screens/home/parts.tsx instead of shortening translations, so the 19 names stay consistent with the Modes row. Only the map uses it; every other header keeps the one-line title. The B3/B8 agents can reuse it for the 'משחק חדש' title. The size steps are driven by onTextLayout, because Android's adjustsFontSizeToFit cannot see mid-word breaks. A long title can therefore take 1-3 extra frames to settle when the map opens.
(2) B27: I used a leading RLM in the he/ar translations rather than FSI-isolating names in code. It works on every platform and version without depending on isolate-aware first-strong detection, and it covers both visible lines and labels. A new test enforces the rule for the levels namespace. The Edit tool wrote the RLMs as literal invisible characters, not ‏ escapes; account.json deleteGoogleBody already does the same. The updated test files also contain literal RLM characters, the same way the repo's tests already use literal LRI/PDI.
(3) B39: besides the gate case, I also handled stage 300 ('תקבל 0 כוכבים.') and the quitCountsAsPlayed=false config. The text follows the same computation as the result's 'לשלב הבא', so the dialog and the result can no longer disagree.
(4) B30: the root cause, the Yoga width cap on an absolute child of a column, is fixed in apps/mobile/src/components/player/Avatar.tsx by a parallel agent's botRoom change made during this workflow. I verified it and added a panel-level assertion, but did not touch Avatar.tsx.

bugs.rootCause: Reanimated 4.5.1 has FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS on. React's own props for LevelResultView's Animated.View always carry the fade's starting opacity 0 (the initial value of useAnimatedStyle). Once an animation settles, Reanimated copies the final value into React's props from a JS setInterval (500 ms, picking up updates 1-2 s old), and it drops the value from its native props registry once it is more than 2 s old (AnimatedPropsRegistry::getUpdatesOlderThanTimestamp). On Android, JS timers stop while the app is in the background, but the fade's callbacks and promises keep running. So when the stage ended just as HOME was pressed, the fade could finish (or finish at the return) without that JS sync ever copying opacity 1 into React. At the return the stale entry was dropped right away. The native view still showed opacity 1, so the result appeared. About 1 s later a React commit under the container (a store update, or another animated child's settled sync) cloned it from React's side with opacity 0, and the whole result went blank. Only id=level-result was left, because its child is at alpha 0. The star pop (StarRow RevealStar) can fail the same way: a star would empty again.
bugs.fix: LevelResultView: the content's Animated.View now also gets a plain `{opacity: 1}` from React once the fade is in. The `entered` state is set from the withTiming completion callback (scheduleOnRN), plus a fallback timer at fade + 400 ms. React's own props then hold the visible state, so no later commit can bring back the 0. The animated style stays attached, so nothing jumps mid-fade. testID level-result-content was added. StarRow RevealStar got the same guard: `popped` is set when the scale sequence ends, and the style becomes opacity 1, scale 1. No timing or visual change in normal use; Reduced Motion keeps its 200 ms fade.

bugs.rootCause: The exact trigger was not reproduced (the tester also failed to reproduce it twice). Two real gaps in the code let a stage's clock run while the app was away. (a) BackgroundPause (game/backgroundPause.ts) assumed the app was in the foreground when it was created (`appActive = true`), and it only learns of AppState from 'change' events after it subscribes. The level session is created only after 'מוכן?' ends and an async step (startLevel awaits the attempt read, then LevelStage mounts). If the app left in that gap, the 'change' was lost. The stage then started unfrozen, and its time limit runs on wall-clock time, so the away time came off the stage. (b) StageRun's useAppActive (play.tsx) read AppState into useState at render and subscribed later in a useEffect. A run mounts anew with every 'לשלב הבא' / 'שוב', and a change between that first render and the subscription was missed. 'מוכן?' then kept counting and could hand off to the stage while away. The previous result briefly showing in the first dump after the return cannot come from React state: the run is re-keyed, so the old result unmounts the moment 'לשלב הבא' is pressed. Most likely the accessibility tree was not yet refreshed after the return; noted, not changed.
bugs.fix: (a) AppStateSource gets an optional `currentState`. BackgroundPause starts `appActive` from it ('background'/'inactive' count as away; 'unknown' counts as active, as elsewhere in the app) and gets a new `started()` method that freezes at once if the app is already away. levelSession calls `this.freeze.started()` right after the stage starts and the bot attaches. A stage that starts while the app is away now starts frozen (covered), and counts 3-2-1 at the return with its full time. (b) play.tsx useAppActive now uses useSyncExternalStore with AppState.currentState, which reads the state again after subscribing, so 'מוכן?' stands still even if the app left before the new run listened. Practice sessions share BackgroundPause; their behaviour is unchanged (they only gain the correct starting appActive). The levelSession doc comment was updated.

rep.notes:
Decisions made on my own:

1. **B26/B35/B48:** the spec does not define what counts as a record for a zero result. I picked: 'שיא חדש!' needs a star (new stars, or a better or equal stored measure in an attempt with a star). A zero-star end shows 'השיא שלך: ★…' only when the best has stars, otherwise no record line. I updated docs/01-SPEC.md §12 and components.md §19.10 to match. The existing QA catalog expectations (levels-result-content, levels-result-your-best) are consistent with this.

2. **B11 root cause** is a Reanimated 4.5.1 mechanism (FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS, which syncs settled values back to React from a JS interval and drops them from the registry after 2 s). It can hit any entrance animation that starts from an invisible value and settles while the app is backgrounded on Android. I hardened the level result container and the star pop (StarRow, shared with the map's pedestal reveal, which is beneficial there too).
   - Other screens may carry the same latent risk: the game results screen entrance, the BossVerdict crown scale (cosmetic only) and the XP count-up.
   - A global alternative would be to set `"reanimated": {"staticFeatureFlags": {"FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS": false}}` in apps/mobile/package.json. That needs a native rebuild and changes every animation, so I did not do it; it is the lead's call.

3. **B28** was not reproducible here either. I closed the two code paths that let a stage clock run while away:
   - BackgroundPause now starts from AppState.currentState and has a new `started()`, called by levelSession right after the start.
   - The play route reads app state through useSyncExternalStore.

   BackgroundPause is shared with practice (game/session.ts). I did not touch game/session.ts. Practice only gains a correct starting appActive, and its tests pass.

issues.problem: The B25/B29 fix stops the overlap at normal text size in Hebrew. But with longer translations on a 360 dp phone, or with larger system text, it cuts the score with an ellipsis or squeezes it to nothing. At very large text the side column, which cannot shrink, can still run over the move dots. So 'nothing overlaps at any score width' is not true, and the fixer's own device check ('repeat with the system font size at maximum') would fail.
issues.evidence:
I measured from the bundled fonts with a small parser of their width tables (Teko_600SemiBold.ttf, Rubik_400Regular.ttf).
- Teko 64: '−0.5' ≈ 109 dp, '−11.5' ≈ 117 dp (about 138 with tabular-nums), '17.5' ≈ 85-99 dp.
- Rubik 13: 'נקודות' 35.7, 'Punkte' 43.1, 'מהלך 1 מתוך 3' 80.5, 'Zug 2 verschenkt' 105.5, 'Jogada 2 queimada' 119.2.

Layout (360 dp phone):
- The HUD row is 328 dp wide (gutterGame 16).
- The moves column has no flexShrink. Gaps are space[4] = 8 and space[3] = 6.
- Room left for the number = (328 − moves − 16)/2 − side − 6.

What that gives:
- pt-BR, just after a burned move (the B25 scenario): room ≈ 48 dp. Even at minimumFontScale 0.5, '−0.5' needs 54.5 dp, so it is ellipsized ('−0…'). German is right at the edge (≈ 54 dp).
- Hebrew at font scale 1.3: room ≈ 51 dp, so even a positive '17.5' is cut.
- Font scale 2.0: room ≈ 0, and the number disappears.
- German at 2.0: the side column ('Punkte' ≈ 86 dp, flexShrink 0, PointHunterHud.tsx:389) is wider than its ≈ 50 dp half, so it overflows into the moves column again.

Why nothing stops this:
- None of these Texts has a font-scale cap (no `scale` / maxFontSizeMultiplier).
- On Android, minimumFontScale applies to the size after font scaling.
- numberOfLines=1 ellipsizes once the minimum is reached (FIT_SCORE, line 362).

The Jest test (ideas.test.tsx B25) checks only props and structure, so it cannot catch this.
issues.suggestion:
Make the score readable under every condition, not just non-overlapping:
- Cap the HUD texts: scale="hud" (×1.35) as the game cards do, and maybe a stricter cap for the Teko number.
- Let the side column shrink or wrap (flexShrink 1, minWidth 0), or put 'נקודות' and the chip under the number instead of beside it.
- Bound the moves text width (maxWidth or numberOfLines 2) so long translations don't eat the halves.
- Check on a 360 dp device in pt-BR and de, and in Hebrew at font scale 1.3 and 2.0.

bugs.rootCause: Reanimated 4.5.1 runs with FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS on. React's props for an animated view keep the animation's starting value: the initial value of useAnimatedStyle/useAnimatedProps, which PropsFilter copies on the first render and always applies last. Reanimated copies a settled value back into React from a 500 ms JS setInterval, and drops it from its native props registry once it is older than 2 s (AnimatedPropsRegistry::getUpdatesOlderThanTimestamp). On Android, JS timers stop in the background, but the animation itself still finishes. So when a stage ended just as HOME was pressed, the result's fade could settle without the sync ever copying opacity 1 into React. At the return the stale entry was dropped. About 1 s later a React commit under the container cloned it from React's side with opacity 0, and the whole result went blank (only id=level-result left). - **StarRow RevealStar:** `popped` is set when the pop ends, and the style becomes opacity 1, scale 1.
- **BossVerdict crown (new, from the review):** `popped` is set from the completion callback, with a fallback at bossWonPopMs + 400 ms, and the style becomes scale 1.
- **XpLine (new, from the review):** a `settled` state is set at revealMs + scoreCount + 400 ms. It remounts CountUpText (key 'settled') with the final value, so React's own initial text is '+20 XP'.

Nothing changes visually in normal use, and Reduced Motion paths are unchanged.

bugs.rootCause: Reanimated 4.5.1 hands React only the start of an animated style. PropsFilter puts the useAnimatedStyle initial values (opacity 0, translateY 12) into the host's React props on every render. The end values live only in the native AnimatedPropsRegistry, and the commit hook re-applies them on each React commit. With FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS (on by default), a JS interval (PropsRegistryGarbageCollector, every 500 ms) asks native for settled updates. ReanimatedModuleProxy::getSettledUpdates calls getUpdatesOlderThanTimestamp(now-1000, now-2000), which first DELETES entries older than 2 s and only then returns the 1-2 s old ones. So if the JS thread is busy through that 1-2 s window, the end is dropped and never synced back to React. The next React commit that clones the node then puts back the initial opacity 0, and the hook has nothing left to re-apply. Fabric clones from React's own tree, so any change inside the card does this, e.g. the account and ratings arriving. That is exactly the window after restartForDirection (Updates.reloadAsync). Home's profile card is the Enter with delay 0, so it ends first, during the busiest JS time after the reload, and its content keeps changing afterwards. 'Spielen' and the rows end later, so they were synced in time. B11 (level result going blank after background) is the same mechanism.
bugs.fix: apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Enter.tsx (Moving): once the entrance has played, its end becomes React's own style. The animated style is replaced by END[kind]: opacity 1, plus translateY 0 or scale 1. 'ended' is set from the withTiming/withSpring finish callbacks through scheduleOnRN, counting both animations for pop and settle. A JS timer (ENTER.endSafetyMs = 1500 ms after the delay) is a safety net in case the UI thread's end never comes. 'play' is now latched in state, so the effect runs once and the safety timer is not cleared when Home's play flips back to false. Every screen that uses Enter gets the fix (Home, Modes, GameType, BotSelect, recent rows, History, Leaderboard, Progress, Login/Splash, game board reveal, ChapterUnlocked). Motion and Reduced Motion are unchanged: Reduced Motion still renders a plain View.

- So a busy JS thread loses the end, and the next React clone resets the view to its start values.
- I did not run it on the phone (no adb was allowed). The fix makes the end state React-owned and does not depend on that window.
- B11 (level result going blank) is the same mechanism. Another agent's LevelResultView already holds opacity 1 in React ('entered'), so the approaches match.
- Any other custom Animated.View whose start is invisible and whose content re-renders after it settles could hit this too. It is worth keeping in mind for overlays.

issues.problem: The B46 fix can still fail on the exact screen and flow it targets: Home's held entrances under the Splash after the restart. The fix makes React's own style END (opacity 1). But Reanimated 4.5.1 appends its own `settledProps` state after the user's style, so they win. For a held Enter, those settledProps can hold the START values. So when the end sync is missed (the fixer's own premise), the card is still put back to opacity 0 / translateY 12 on the next React clone. The claim 'a later render never brings back the start' does not hold in this path.
issues.evidence:
1) node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/createAnimatedComponent/AnimatedComponent.tsx:542-543 renders `style: [...flattenArray(filteredProps.style), this.state.settledProps]`, so settledProps override END. In _syncStylePropsBackToReact (l.218-224) settledProps are only ever merged in, with the comment 'TODO(future): revert changes when animated styles are detached'.
2) For a 'rise' Enter, the mapper's first UI run writes the start into the native registry with a timestamp. useAnimatedStyle.ts:304 calls updateProps because shallowEqual (hook/utils.ts:20-35) sees the new `transform` array !== state.last's. The write goes through ReanimatedModuleProxy.cpp:283-291 -> AnimatedPropsRegistry::update, which sets timestampMap_.
3) Home holds every Enter with play={enter} (HomeScreen.tsx:182/203/214/229/248) while the sign-in loads under the Splash. Nothing refreshes that start entry during the hold. If the hold lasts >=1 s with JS idle (async auth I/O), PropsRegistryGarbageCollector (500 ms interval) gets it from getSettledUpdates (age 1-2 s, ReanimatedModuleProxy.cpp:662) and syncs {opacity:0, transform:[{translateY:12}]} into the card's settledProps.
4) Then the account and ratings arrive and JS is busy, which is the fixer's premise: the end entry is deleted unsynced (AnimatedPropsRegistry.cpp:49, 72-82). The next React commit sends [style, END, settledProps(start)] and the card is hidden again.
5) Jest has no native registry, so Enter.test.tsx and homeEntrance.test.tsx cannot exercise this path. (They do fail on the old Enter: I ran them against the base version with a moduleNameMapper, 3 failures.)
issues.suggestion: Make sure a held Enter never leaves a start entry in the registry long enough to be synced. Option 1: while `!started`, render the start as a plain React style and attach the animated style only once it starts. Watch the PropsFilter first-render-only initial props (PropsFilter.tsx:44-51): a handle attached later gets {} from React, so keep the plain START in the style array on that render to avoid a one-frame flash. Option 2, global, covers B11 and any other Animated.View too: turn off FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS via apps/mobile/package.json "reanimated": {"staticFeatureFlags": {...: false}} (read by scripts/reanimated_utils.rb:82). This needs a native rebuild. Either way, add a test that simulates a settledProps start sync, or document the native-only check in deviceCheck.

bugs.rootCause: Reanimated 4.5.1 hands React only the start of an animated style. PropsFilter puts the useAnimatedStyle initial values (opacity 0, translateY 12) into React's props on every render. What the UI thread drew lives only in the native AnimatedPropsRegistry, and the commit hook applies it again on each React commit. With FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS (on by default), a JS interval (PropsRegistryGarbageCollector, every 500 ms) asks for settled updates. getSettledUpdates(now-1000, now-2000) first DELETES entries older than 2 s, and only then returns the 1-2 s old ones. So when JS is busy through that window, the end is dropped and never synced back. The next React commit then puts back opacity 0, and the hook has nothing left to apply. That is the window right after restartForDirection. Home's card is the delay-0 Enter whose content keeps changing (the account and ratings arrive). Review finding (confirmed in the sources): AnimatedComponent.render appends state.settledProps AFTER the user's style (AnimatedComponent.tsx:538-543), and settledProps are only ever merged in. A held Enter had its animated style on the view during the Splash hold. The mapper's first run writes the start into the registry (the transform array is never shallow-equal), and ViewDescriptorsSet.add force-runs the updater when a style attaches. After 1 s of idle JS, that start could be synced into settledProps, and it would then override the END style the earlier fix rendered.
bugs.fix:
apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Enter.tsx (Moving): the style is animated only while the part moves. Before and after, React owns the start and the end.
- While held (not started): style = [style, START]. START comes from startOf(kind, distance): opacity 0 plus translateY or scale. No animated style is on the view, so the registry never holds this view's start and nothing can be synced back.
- Once started: [style, START, animated]. START stays under the handle, because a handle attached after the first render gets {} from PropsFilter, and that would flash one frame.
- Once ended: [style, END[kind]], as in the earlier fix. 'ended' comes from the withTiming/withSpring finish callbacks (scheduleOnRN), or from the ENTER.endSafetyMs JS timer as a safety net. 'play' is latched in state.
- All screens using Enter get this: Home, Modes, GameType, BotSelect, recent rows, History, Leaderboard, Progress, Login/Splash and the game board reveal.

final.notes:
How I handled each review issue:

1. HIGH, B46: held Enter start synced into settledProps. Agreed and fixed.
- Confirmed in the 4.5.1 sources:
  - AnimatedComponent.tsx:538-543 renders settledProps after the user's style.
  - _syncStylePropsBackToReact only ever merges.
  - ViewDescriptorsSet.add calls updater(true) when a style attaches.
  - styleUpdater's shallowEqual fails on transform arrays.
- The fix is the reviewer's option 1. While held, the start is a plain React style and no animated style is on the view. The animated style attaches only once the part starts, with START kept under it, because PropsFilter hands a late-attached handle {} and that would flash one frame.
- enterSettled.test.tsx models the sync with the flag on. It fails on the earlier version and passes now.
- Residual edge, not covered: if the UI thread stalls for 1 s or more in the middle of an entrance (e.g. the app goes to the background mid-animation), a mid value could be synced, and if the end is then also dropped, it would override END.
- The global cure is the reviewer's option 2: "reanimated": {"staticFeatureFlags": {"FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS": false}} in apps/mobile/package.json. It needs a native rebuild and changes every animated view in the app. I did not do it: it can't be verified without a device, and it is outside this area's minimal change. It also bears on B11 (another agent's area). This is a decision for the lead.

2. MEDIUM, B23 dropped the 'בדירוג זמני' words. Agreed.
- The full line is back in the pinned row. Stacking the chip and allowing 2 lines fix the Hebrew case.
- The test now checks the full line against the stacked column: 1 line on the A16, at most 2 at 360 dp.
- List rows, the accessibility label and the QA catalog ('מתחת לשם: סמל הליגה, או בדירוג זמני · רמה N'; 'בצד השני: הדירוג') all agree, so the catalog needs no change.
- The components.md §5 line is updated to match.

3. LOW, long languages in the pinned row. Not fixed: it needs a layout decision from Moshe, so B23 is closed for Hebrew only, not for all 19 languages.
- Name column with the chip stacked, at 360/384 dp (font-metric estimate): he 86/110, en 47/71, es 34/58, de 33/57, fr 39/63, it 35/59, nl 35/59, pl 38/62, pt-BR 39/63, id 45/69, vi 31/55, ru 20/44, ar 21/45. The CJK, ko, tr and th columns are 62-82/86-106.
- In about 12 languages, 'Provisional rating · Level 14' cannot fit 2 lines, because single words are wider than the column. The name itself may also be cut there.
- The cause is the 'Play' button (81-133 dp) and the rating's width next to it. Options for Moshe: a narrower or icon-only play button in the pinned row (the design, Leaderboard.dc.html, has a 62 px button), or play above the row. This needs to go into the handoff.

4. LOW, ProfileCard.tsx CRLF. Fixed: converted to LF with no content change, and prettier --check is clean.

For the lead:

It also touches Reanimated internals (AnimatedComponent.prototype, PropsRegistryGarbageCollector.syncPropsBackToReact). It is written against 4.5.1, so a Reanimated upgrade may need it adjusted.

issues.problem: The new `fitTitle` layout gives the New Game header title a width of 0 on the device, in every language including Hebrew. `styles.titles` still has `flex: 1`, and the fix only layers `titlesFirst: { flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: 'auto' }` on top of it. In Yoga, `processFlexBasis()` returns `points(0)` whenever `flexBasis` is auto and `flex > 0`, so the explicit `flexBasis: 'auto'` does not override `flex: 1`. The title box therefore has basis 0 and grow 0, and Me (`flexGrow 1, flexBasis 0`) takes the whole row. The title vanishes or ends in a lone '…', and my name always shows. So B3 ("Новая партия" whole) and B8 (id "Pertandingan baru" whole) are not fixed on the phone; the screen is worse than before. The Jest tests only check the style props (`toMatchObject({flexGrow:0, flexShrink:1, flexBasis:'auto'})`) and arithmetic constants (modesFit TITLE_ROOM), so they pass while the real layout is broken.
issues.evidence: parts.tsx:253 `titles: { flex: 1, minWidth: 0, ... }`; parts.tsx:256 `titlesFirst: { flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: 'auto' }`, applied as `[styles.titles, fitTitle && styles.titlesFirst]` (parts.tsx:88). node_modules/react-native/ReactCommon/yoga/yoga/node/Node.cpp:329-338 (RN 0.86.3): `if (!flexBasis.isAuto() ...) return flexBasis; if (style_.flex().isDefined() && style_.flex().unwrap() > 0.0f) return useWebDefaults() ? auto : StyleSizeLength::points(0);`. YogaStylableProps.cpp:144-147 sets flex, flexGrow and flexBasis independently, and RN never enables useWebDefaults. I ran the header with yoga-layout 3.2.1 (row 328, back 44, gap 12, Me as in ModesScreen.tsx:754): as shipped, a 197 dp title (ru) gives `titles width: 0, me 260`; a 263 dp title (id) gives `titles width: 0`; a 120 dp title (he) gives `titles width: 0`. With `flex: 0` added to titlesFirst: ru 197 / me 63, he 120 / me 140, and id is clamped to 226 as the fixer intended.
issues.suggestion: In `titlesFirst`, also cancel the inherited flex, e.g. `{ flex: 0, flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: 'auto' }`, or don't apply `styles.titles`' `flex: 1` when `fitTitle` is on. Add a test assertion that the flattened style of the title box has no positive `flex`, e.g. `expect(StyleSheet.flatten(titles.props.style).flex ?? 0).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0)`, so the test would catch this. Then do the B3/B8 device check (ru, fr, id, he) before calling it fixed.

One high-severity regression:
- **The New Game header title will be 0 wide on the device, in every language, Hebrew included.** The new `fitTitle` style keeps the inherited `flex: 1`. Yoga's `processFlexBasis` turns an explicit `flexBasis: 'auto'` back into basis 0 when `flex > 0`. With flexGrow 0, the title box gets nothing, and Me (flexGrow 1, basis 0) takes the whole row.
- I reproduced it with yoga-layout 3.2.1: Russian, Indonesian and Hebrew titles all get width 0. Adding `flex: 0` gives the intended 197, 226 and 120 dp.
- So B3 (the cut titles) and the Indonesian title in B8 are not fixed on the phone; the screen is worse than before. The Jest tests only check style props and arithmetic, so they cannot catch this.

Low-severity items:
- Spanish, Arabic and Vietnamese offline wording now reads like a status ('no connection') rather than 'works offline'. The fixer says the ar and vi changes were driven by over-wide width estimates.
- When the name is hidden, the header's end item has nothing a screen reader can read.
- Italian "Home" and Dutch "live" are not in the glossary that the style guides cite.

bugs.rootCause: There were three causes, all confirmed in ModesScreen.tsx and in the sweep dumps. (1) The header title box had flex:1 (flex-basis 0), so the title only got what was left after Me (the name plus the avatar). With the QA name "אורי" (22 dp) beside the avatar, "Новая партия" (197 dp) and "Nouvelle partie" (212 dp) were cut in a 226 dp row. (2) The two chips on the bot and solo rows ("Unrated" + "Works offline") share one column, and in ru and fr they did not fit side by side. On the device, es also wrapped even at 384 dp (sweep es-2new.xml: the two chips are on y=1217 and y=1296). So the second chip went onto a new line, each row grew 28 dp, and staged practice slid under the friends footer. No test checked the two chips together. (3) The leftover 4 px (2 dp) scroll in de/th/ja/pl/nl comes from the QA emulation. wm size 720x1560 at density 320 keeps the A16's 100 px status bar, which is 50 dp. The content (551 dp) plus the footer and nav came out 2 dp taller than the screen, because the budget test assumed a 32 dp status bar. Review fix: the first version of fitTitle laid `titlesFirst {flexGrow 0, flexShrink 1, flexBasis 'auto'}` over `titles {flex: 1}`. In Yoga (RN 0.86.3 Node::processFlexBasis), a positive `flex` turns an auto basis into 0. So the title box got basis 0 and grow 0, Me took the whole row, and the title would have been 0 wide in every language, Hebrew too. I reproduced it with yoga-layout 3.2.1: as shipped, the ru, id and he titles were all 0 wide.

final.notes:
Review issues, in order:
1. HIGH, title 0 wide (fixed, confirmed). In Yoga's processFlexBasis (RN 0.86.3), a positive `flex` turns an auto basis into 0, so laying titlesFirst over `titles {flex:1}` left the title box at basis 0 and grow 0. I split the style rather than counting on overrides. `titles` no longer has `flex`. Headers without fitTitle get `titlesRest {flex: 1}`, so the other ~17 screens using ScreenHeader are unchanged. With fitTitle the box gets `titlesFirst`, which has no `flex` at all, plus a comment saying why. Regression check: ModesAndGameType asserts that the flattened title box has no positive flex; this fails on the reviewed version. yoga-layout is not a repo dependency, so a real Yoga layout test was not added; the reviewer's script (scratchpad yoga-scripts/header.mjs) confirms the numbers above. The lead should still do the B3 (a) Hebrew check on the phone.
2. LOW, Me accessibility and pop-in (fixed). Me is one accessible View labelled with my name (accessible only when there is a name), so the name is still read when only the avatar shows. Before the first layout the name now shows, so Hebrew and most languages get no pop-in. A tight language (ru/fr/id) can show the name squeezed for one frame before it hides. Me's width does not depend on its content (flexBasis 0), so this never moves the title. The name-hiding rule itself is still a decision for Moshe to confirm (see 5 below).
3. LOW, es/ar/vi offline wording (partly disagree, with evidence). es: the device proves the long wording wraps. The run-2 sweep (es-2new.xml, 384 dp A16) has \"Sin puntuación\" and \"Funciona sin conexión\" on two lines (y 1217 vs 1296 px; 88 + 130 dp of text, a 260 dp row). The capability phrasings I measured do not fit 226: \"Juega sin conexión\" 241, \"También sin conexión\" 255. \"Juega sin red\" fits, but \"sin red\" is also the idiom for 'without a safety net'. \"Sin conexión\" next to \"Sin puntuación\" reads as a property of the mode, the standard Spanish feature label (\"Disponible sin conexión\"). Kept. ar/vi: the reviewer is right that the long wording fit on the Android device: ar row 186 dp, vi row 220 dp of 226 (ar-2new.xml, vi-2new.xml). The shared estimator puts them at 241 and 251: fontMetrics measures Arabic's isolated forms, plus 10%, and textWidth adds 10% for vi on top of a wide Latin estimate. Repo policy requires every real language to pass, and iOS's system font for Vietnamese is wider than Roboto. No capability phrasing I measured fits that estimate: ar \"يعمل دون إنترنت\" 246, \"متاح دون اتصال\" 238; vi \"Ngoại tuyến\" 231, \"Chơi không mạng\" 259. So ar \"دون اتصال\" and vi \"Không mạng\" stay; each pairs with its row's \"دون تصنيف\" / \"Không xếp hạng\" as a property. I did not change the shared estimator (layout.ts / fontMetrics.ts), because ~10 agents' layout tests depend on it. Suggested follow-up: shape Arabic joined forms in fontMetrics and calibrate the vi margin, then restore \"يعمل دون اتصال\" and \"Không cần mạng\".

bugs.rootCause: Cell.tsx FlashLayer started its hold with withDelay(holdMs, fade) and did not pass a reduceMotion argument. Reanimated's withDelay defaults to ReduceMotion.System. When the phone's own animation scale is 0 (the QA phones are set this way with adb; Reanimated reads transition_animation_scale), the 300 ms hold was skipped, so the reduced red frame started its 200 ms fade at once and was visible for under ~130 ms. The inner withTiming already used ReduceMotion.Never, which is why only the hold disappeared. The lock release at the same moment does not cut the frame: FlashLayer stays mounted for FLASH_CLEAR_MS (900 ms), and the test covers that rerender. bugs.rootCause: Several clock accessibility labels changed every second. SoloHud's stats group label was 'זמן 3:12 · מהלך שיא…'. Each level HUD clock (Box, Puzzle, Chain, SpotError, Race, Duel, PointHunter, and Find's ring label) built its label from secondsOf(now). Every change of contentDescription sends a TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED event, so uiautomator never got a quiet second, and TalkBack got a useless event every second. The visible clock digits are a TextView whose text changes every second, and Android's TextView.setText posts a content-change event too (I am fairly sure of this AOSP behaviour, but could not run it on a phone). So fixing the labels alone may not be enough for uiautomator.

The best-move stat keeps its own label, which changes only with a new best. The now-unused key game:hud.timeLabel is removed from all 19 locales. Level HUDs: new helper format.ts clockLabelSeconds(ms, 'elapsed' | 'left') with CLOCK_LABEL_STEP_S = 5. Elapsed time rounds down to 5 s; time left rounds up to 5 s and is exact in its last 5 s (never '0' while time is left). All 8 clock labels use it, so a label changes every 5 s and keeps its wording (limit and unit). The lock timers (cell label, lock strip, card activity, hit and reconnect seconds) are unchanged on purpose: they last 8–18 s, the exact seconds are the information, and the ring and bar animate during a lock anyway.

Decisions, in Hebrew:
- B15/B50 (מקלדת): במקום לחשב צבעים מראש לכל צבע של המקש (רקע, מסגרת, ספרה, ספירה, שפה) ולהנפיש אותם, כל מקש נשאר אטום, ומעליו "וילון" בצבע color.bg עם שקיפות 1−(שקיפות המקש × רמת השורה).
  - על המסך זה בדיוק החישוב המוקדם מעל הרקע, כלומר אותו מראה.

On Android, a TextView text change sends a window-content-changed event. `uiautomator dump` waits for about 1 s of quiet, so a change every second is enough to block the idle state. (2) The fixer left every lock-seconds label as it was. The cell label (`{seconds}` for myLock and oppLock) and the LockStrip label and accessibilityValue change every second while any lock is held. Against a bot or a ranked rival, a lock is held almost all the time. issues.problem: clockLabelSeconds rounds time left up to the 5 s step: 6.2 s left is read as '10 seconds'. Elapsed time rounds down, so the label for 14 s elapsed out of a 30 s limit says 10. Either way, a screen-reader user can hear up to about 4 s more time than is really left. Spec 24 (line 1751) says the time left is read aloud for stage play.
issues.evidence: format.ts:95 `return left <= step ? left : Math.ceil(left / step) * step;`. The test expects `clockLabelSeconds(6200, 'left') === 10`.
issues.suggestion: Round time left down to the step, which never goes below 1 while time is left, because it is exact in the last step. Then the label never promises more time than there is.

rev.summary:
I checked the game-area fixes against the diff from af4c8a5, the Reanimated 4.5.1 source and the docs. Tests, type-check and lint are clean: 11 suites / 429 new and changed tests, plus wider runs of 81 suites / 1581 tests and 52 game suites / 853 tests, all pass. tsc --noEmit and eslint --max-warnings 0 on the changed files are clean, and i18n:check has 0 errors.

What holds:
- B36: the cause is confirmed in Reanimated's code. withDelay with no reduceMotion takes the system value, and on Android that comes from transition_animation_scale, so the delay is skipped. The same batch's B37 symptoms suggest the phone's animations were off during that run.
- B15/B50: the color.bg veil over an opaque key gives the same result as the old opacity, the keys are opaque, and the tests pin it.
- B12: Choice, Segmented and the streak chip are opaque.
- B45: both halves can shrink and their words wrap, with per-language Yoga tests.
- B47: fixed for de, ru and th.
- The key removal is consistent across all 19 locales, and none of the peer-session files were touched.

Medium issues that remain:
1. The 2P "הפרעה" button, in the fixer's own area, keeps a translucent interfere.bg fill straight over the ambient digits. This is the same kind of bug as B12/B50, and it was neither fixed nor listed.
2. Q1 is only partly done. The visible clock Text and the lock-seconds labels still change every second, so uiautomator will most likely still not reach an idle state on the game screens.
3. B47 still cuts the rival's status row in 7 locales (ar, es, pt-BR, fr, tr, vi, nl), although D124's "shorten first" is available.

Low issues: Choice now paints color.bg inside the pseudo-language surface card; some translucent HUD chips and the in-game ReactionPicker withDelay are missing from the follow-up list; the 5 s clock label rounds time left up.

bugs.rootCause: Corrected from the earlier report. In Cell.tsx, FlashLayer started the reduced frame's 300 ms hold with withDelay(holdMs, fade) and passed no reduceMotion argument. Reanimated's withDelay then uses ReduceMotion.System, which Reanimated resolves from ReducedMotionManager. The app's MotionPolicy (theme/MotionPolicy.tsx, mounted first in app/_layout) renders <ReducedMotionConfig mode={app decision}>. When the setting 'הפחתת תנועה' is 'מופעלת', that calls ReducedMotionManager.setEnabled(true) (checked in node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/component/ReducedMotionConfig.tsx). So withDelay counted as reduced and skipped the hold: the static frame went straight into its 200 ms fade and was visible for under ~130 ms. This happens with the phone's own animation settings at their defaults; a phone with its animations off also triggers it. The inner withTiming already used ReduceMotion.Never, which is why only the hold disappeared. The lock release at the same moment does not cut the frame (FlashLayer stays mounted for FLASH_CLEAR_MS).
bugs.fix: Done in the earlier round, kept: ReduceMotion.Never on every withDelay that is part of a chosen variant. That covers FlashLayer (the frame's hold and the wrong digit's shrink), Score.tsx (×2), ActivityLine MistakesText, ReactionLayer's reduced float and FlightLayer (×4). This round I corrected the root-cause comments in Cell.tsx and in the test, which had blamed only the phone's animation scale.

It sets the app setting to 'on' and ReducedMotionManager.setEnabled(true), which is exactly what MotionPolicy does. Opacity is 1 at 280 ms, mid-fade at 400 ms and 0 at 600 ms, and it fails without the fix (checked in the earlier round). Re-run: components/board, 47 + 23 cases, green.

bugs.rootCause:
On Android, any per-second change sends TYPE_WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED, and `uiautomator dump` needs about 1 s with no accessibility events. Two kinds of per-second change were found:
(1) A changed accessibilityLabel (contentDescription). That was the earlier diagnosis.
(2) The visible clock text. RN 0.86 renders Text as ReactTextView (enablePreparedTextLayout defaults to false in ReactNativeFeatureFlagsDefaults.kt), and TextView.setText notifies CONTENT_CHANGE_TYPE_TEXT. So the solo clock sent an event every second even after the earlier label fix, as the reviewer said.
Per-second labels were: the solo time label, the 8 level HUD clocks, every lock's seconds in the cell label (myLock and oppLock), and the LockStrip label and progressbar value. A View transform or layout change also emits (View.setTranslation/setScale/setFrame call notifySubtreeAccessibilityStateChangedIfNeeded). That fits the earlier device finding that a looping avatar idle (Animated.View transforms) blocked idle, while the ambient layer (an opaque Skia SurfaceView) does not.
bugs.fix:
- The solo practice's clock is now drawn as SVG paths. New ClockDigits (components/clock/ClockDigits.tsx) uses Teko 600 outlines for 0–9 and ':' from new scripts/gen-clock-glyphs.mjs → clockGlyphs.generated.ts. lib/ttf.mjs gained advance() and vertical(), additive and lazy.
  - It sits in the cellRef line box, with the baseline placed by RN's half-leading model.
  - The digits are tabular, so the box never resizes while it runs (a resize would be a layout event too).
  - It grows with the system font scale like the Text it replaces, and is hidden from screen readers.
  - Changing a path's `d` only invalidates the drawing: no text view, no content-description change.
- The time stat has a label again. game:hud.timeLabel is restored in all 19 locales with the 1.1.0 strings, so the net text change is none. The label is 'זמן 3:10', stepped to 5 s: clockLabelSeconds rounds elapsed time down.
- clockLabelSeconds 'left' now rounds down (reviewer, low): it never says more time than the clock shows, and it is exact in the last 5 s. A new labelSecondsLeft() does the same for whole seconds.
- Lock seconds: the cell label (board/labels.ts, my lock and others' locks), the LockStrip group label and the progressbar's accessibilityValue use labelSecondsLeft. That is 5 s steps, every second only in the last 5 (12→'10', 9→'5', then 4, 3, 2, 1). The pill and strip text still show every second, and the lock/3 s/release announcements stay exact (components.md §10 'Do not announce every second').
- Docs: components.md §3.6 (solo time), §10, §11.5, §19.6.
- Not done, and why:
