final.testsRun:
All runs used --maxWorkers=2. Everything passed except one suite that fails because of a peer's change.
- npx jest components/player + components/board + components/clock + components/dev + screens/home + theme + __tests__/clockLabels: 48 suites, 906 tests, green.
- npx jest screens/game + screens/levels + src/__tests__: all green except:

  - numberPlurals.test.ts: fails on levels:hud.duel.meLabel/botLabel, where a peer added an RLM to he/levels.json. Not mine.
- Re-runs after the last change:
  - components/player + GameScreen* + components/dev + contrast: 27 suites green (numberPlurals is the same peer failure).
  - The group and online-group game tests, PlayerCard and opaqueChoices: green.
  - friendsDocs, levelsSpecDocs, widthBudget (66), i18nParity, i18nCheck, screens/progress and PseudoLanguageSettings: green.
- npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit: clean.
- npx eslint --max-warnings 0 on every file I changed or created: clean.
- prettier --check on them: clean. I ran prettier --write only on my own new files and on files whose only diffs were my lines (I checked first).
- npm run i18n:check: 0 errors, the 2 existing plural warnings.
- node apps/mobile/scripts/gen-clock-glyphs.mjs: the generated file matches Prettier, and a re-run writes the same bytes.
final.notes:
החלטות וממצאים:

**תגובה להערות הסוקר**
- **בינוני 1, כפתור 'הפרעה' ב־2P שקוף:** תוקן.
  - המילוי והלחיצה אטומים (opaqueOver).
  - במצב חסום יש וילון בצבע color.bg ב־0.5 מעל הכפתור האטום.
  - ניסיתי קודם צבעים מחושבים מראש, אבל a11yAudit דורש שצבע טקסט יהיה מה־tokens. לכן וילון: הטקסט נשאר בצבעי התמה, והמראה זהה ל־opacity 0.5 מעל הרקע.
- **בינוני 2, Q1:** השעון של אימון לבד מצויר עכשיו ב־SVG, והתוויות של שניות הנעילה מתעדכנות בצעדים. פירוט בסעיף Q1.
  - נשאר: בזמן שאני מחזיק נעילה, הטקסט והפס של הנעילה עדיין משתנים כל שנייה. במסכי השלבים, StarsBar מונפש כל הזמן.
  - לכן Q1 מסומן partial. ההכרעה במכשיר.
  - בנוסף: כלי ה־QA (‏adb.ts ‏`ui`) מחזיר dump ישן כש־uiautomator נכשל. כדאי שייכשל בקול. זה שרת, אחר, לא נגעתי.
- **בינוני 3, B47:** קוצר לפי D124 ב־7 השפות, ורשימת החריגים נמחקה מהבדיקה. "Baltala" נבחר כי אין בטורקית קיצור טבעי ל־"Düşünüyor". "Sabotaj" לא נכנס (0.72), והוא שם עצם, בעוד שהמדריך דורש ציווי לכפתור.
- **נמוך:**
  - Choice עם ground: תוקן.
  - צ'יפים: BoxHud, PuzzleHud ו־FindHud תוקנו.
  - עיגול הזמן שנותר: תוקן, עכשיו כלפי מטה.
  - ReactionPicker לא תוקן בכוונה. ה־withDelay שם רץ רק בענף התנועה המלאה, ושם MotionPolicy פותר את System להחלטת האפליקציה (לא מופחת), כך שה־delay לא מדולג. זה לא באג.

**תיקון הסיבה של B36**
- לא הגדרת האנימציות של הטלפון. MotionPolicy מעביר את הגדרת 'מופעלת' ל־ReducedMotionConfig, ואז withDelay בלי Never מדלג על ההמתנה, גם בטלפון רגיל.
- התיקון עצמו נשאר.

**ממצא חדש, B47 כשהיריב מחזיק משבצת**
- בשורה של היריב, כשהוא "בוחר · A8", לפי מודל המדידה כמעט בכל השפות משמאל לימין אין מקום גם לטבעת, למילה וגם למילה על הכפתור ב־0.75. באנגלית, גם בחלוקה אופטימלית יוצא 0.70.
- כיום (מהסבב הקודם) המילה של היריב נשמרת, והמילה על הכפתור מתכווצת ועלולה להיחתך ("Interf…"). האייקון נשאר.
- פתרון מלא דורש החלטה של משה: כפתור עם אייקון בלבד בכרטיס 2P (בניגוד ל־§8.1), או שינוי רוחב או ריפוד של הכפתור. לא שיניתי.

**נמצא ולא תוקן (אזורים אחרים, או מחוץ להיקף)**
- CardIconButton (כניעה ותגובות בכרטיס שלי): opacity 0.4 או 0.5 כשהוא מושבת או בהשהיית התגובות, וגם עמעום הכרטיס (dimmedCard). אותה תקלת שקיפות מול הספרות המשוטטות.
- PointHunterHud (צ'יפים iconBg.danger ו־dangerSubtle): סוכן אחר עורך את הקובץ.
- SpotErrorHud lensFill: מילוי מונפש, ייתכן שהשקיפות מכוונת.
- הרשימה הקודמת (ResultsScreen, BossBand, OfflineBanner, עיגולי אייקונים) עדיין פתוחה.

bugs.rootCause: Measured on RF8Y60PP2XZ with atrace and gfxinfo framestats, read-only. The long frame is the UI thread's draw pass, not the fade. Two things combine there. (1) react-native-svg sends a topSvgLayout event for every shape (path, g, circle) the first time it draws it. One static avatar has 50–130 shapes. On Android, Reanimated 4.5 (NodesManager.onEventDispatch → performNonLayoutOperations → getPendingUpdates) re-applies the last props of every view it animated in the last ~2 s, once per event. So each new SVG shape costs time in proportion to how many views animated recently. (2) If one of those views was deleted in the same frame, Reanimated still holds it until reportMount, which runs after the frame. Every new shape then fails on it: RetryableMountingLayerException plus a full stack trace logged by Log.w, about 1 ms each. The real app trigger is in AvatarArt. Home's avatar is a stage (AVATAR_STAGES.home). When Home lost focus (useScreenFocused), it swapped its layered stack (Animated.View LayerNodes) for one static SvgXml under the new screen, and swapped back on return. Measured: Home→Settings had one 274 ms draw with 124 new shapes (Home's static avatar) and 234 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed' (two stale eye-layer tags from the blink × 117 events). Home→Modes had draws of 131 ms (Modes' own 278 shapes) and 310 ms (Home's 124 shapes, 248 failures). Back had an 87 ms draw (142 layer shapes remounted), plus JS for nativeLayers and 8 SvgXml. On top of that, HomeScreen called useScreenFocused() at its top level, so the whole Home tree re-rendered on every blur and focus, even after its entrance. The same delete-a-fresh-layer-in-the-frame-that-draws-a-new-picture pattern also happened at the end of every avatar reaction in game (layers → static), in the avatar picker (old tile idle→off) and in FighterPreview (avatar id change).
bugs.fix: 1) apps/mobile/src/avatars/AvatarArt.tsx: a stage (idle && !reduce) keeps its layered stack while its screen is covered. It only stops its beats, so there is no static↔layered swap on any screen change from Home. 2) AvatarArt: stacks it no longer shows are kept as the same React instances in one keyed list. This covers a motion that ended, a new avatar/size/crop, and a different set of moving layers. The old stack is hidden (opacity 0, plans none, at rest) for LAYERS_RETIRE_MS = 4000 ms, then unmounted. Reanimated drops a view 2–2.5 s after its last frame, so by then nothing holds it and deleting it can't fail. The new picture still shows at once, exactly as before. No visual change other than speed.

bugs.rootCause: The QA guess was not quite right: the previous character's animations are cancelled on unmount (LayerNode's effect cleanup calls cancelAnimation). The failures come from the mechanism in B14. The lab keys every AvatarArt by character id. So one commit deleted all the old character's moving layers and mounted the new character's avatars. Those are about 18 at 96/64/36/22 px plus 20 expression faces at 52 px, roughly 3,000 SVG shapes. The deleted layers include the stage's idle layers and the grid's endless expression gimmicks (≥48 px), and Reanimated still held all of them. Each of the ~3,000 shapes drawn in that frame re-applied that list and failed on every deleted tag, each failure with a full stack trace (lab-reanimated-excerpt.txt: VirtualView.setClientRect → FabricEventDispatcher → NodesManager.onEventDispatch → performNonLayoutOperations → synchronouslyUpdateUIProps). That is tens of thousands of logged exceptions per switch, minutes of UI-thread time, hence the ANR. AvatarArt had the same pattern elsewhere: layers → still picture at the end of every motion (the lab's motion buttons, in-game reactions), idle off, and avatar id change. That is fixed under B14.

After SWITCH_FRAMES (2 requestAnimationFrame ticks, so that commit is mounted and Reanimated has dropped the deleted views): 'still', the new character is drawn with reduceMotion, so it is static and adds nothing to Reanimated's list. rep.notes: Decisions: (1) LAYERS_RETIRE_MS = 4000 ms. Reanimated's settled-props garbage collection drops a view's props 2 s after its last frame and polls every 500 ms, so 2.5 s is the floor; 4000 leaves room for a busy JS thread. While kept, the hidden stacks cost a few bitmaps and views and draw nothing. (2) A covered stage keeps its layers (no beats) instead of turning into one picture. motion.md §4.10's 'idles only while its screen is shown' still holds, and the look is identical. (3) Lab switch: 2 frames per step, the smallest gap that guarantees the deleting commit is mounted first (rAF fires in the UI frame's TIMERS phase, after DISPATCH_UI). Expected gains: about 270 ms less for Home→Settings and about 90 ms less for Back, plus the JS of Home's re-render and of rebuilding the avatar. Home→Modes loses its 310 ms frame (≈0.8–1.05 s → ≈0.45–0.6 s). No more ~250 logged exceptions per change of screen from Home, no hitch at the end of in-game avatar reactions, and no ANR in the lab (a switch ≈1 s, spread over separate frames). B14 is 'partial' because some remains on 'משחק חדש': about 250–300 ms of JS building the screen (two SvgXml avatars are parsed and turned into ~250 React SVG elements), and about 130 ms to draw its own 278 shapes for the first time, each still re-applying what Reanimated holds. The real fix is native and I did not do it: a patch to react-native-reanimated NodesManager.onEventDispatch, skipping the flush when no worklet handler waits for the event, as it already does off the UI thread; or to react-native-svg, not sending topSvgLayout without a listener. Either needs patch-package plus a native build and its own testing. Follow-ups I left on purpose: useConnectivityWatch returns the whole store, so each /health check re-renders Home and Modes twice (after the first frame, so the transition start isn't delayed). A screen that unmounts avatars that just moved while another screen mounts many SVGs (e.g. game→results) can still hit one stale frame; that is outside AvatarArt's control. Shared files: AvatarArt.tsx already carried another agent's B10 change (accessibilityValue only under NODE_ENV test), and I kept it. The other useScreenFocused callers (LevelMapScreen, LevelNode, app/results/[id]) are unaffected; the argument defaults to true. No UI strings and no locales changed.

issues.problem: This test claims Home does not render again when it is covered or shown, but it mocks useFocusEffect so the effect runs only on mount, which hides the renders the real app still does on every return to Home. In the app, each focus runs refreshHome. That calls usePracticeHistory.refresh, which sets status 'loading' synchronously and then sets a new `recent` array with status 'ready'. HomeScreen subscribes to both, so Home renders at least twice on every Back. The report's claim that 'after the entrance has played a change of screen never re-renders Home' holds for blur only, so the expected gain on Back is overstated.
issues.evidence: homeTransitions.test.tsx:35-40 mocks `useFocusEffect: (effect) => useEffect(effect, [effect])`. HomeScreen.tsx:112-121: useFocusEffect calls refreshHome. HomeScreen.tsx:312-319: refreshHome awaits usePracticeHistory.getState().refresh(). state/practiceHistory.ts:28 sets `set({ status: 'loading' })` and :37 sets `set(recent ? { recent, status: 'ready' } ...)`. HomeScreen.tsx:81-82 subscribes to `recent` and `status`.
issues.suggestion: Either narrow the test name and the PERF.md wording to blur, or stop the focus refresh from re-rendering an unchanged Home. Two ways: keep the status as it is when a list is already loaded (stale-while-revalidate), and keep the old `recent` array when its ids are unchanged. Or defer the refresh until the transition ends. Then add a test where the focus effect really runs on each focus.

issues.problem: useRetiredStacks has a hidden failure mode. Its unmount cleanup clears every timeout but never empties the timers Map. If effects re-run without the component unmounting (Fast Refresh in dev, StrictMode, or a future React <Activity> for inactive screens), the [retired] effect finds every stack still in the Map and starts no new timer. Those hidden stacks would then stay until the AvatarArt unmounts. This does not happen in the current release app: there is no StrictMode in app/_layout.tsx, and expo-router's native stack does not use Activity.
issues.evidence: AvatarArt.tsx:265-281: `if (!live.has(s)) live.set(s, setTimeout(...))`, and the cleanup is `return () => live.forEach(clearTimeout);`, which does not call `live.clear()`.
issues.suggestion: Call `live.clear()` in the cleanup (or delete each entry as it is cleared), and create the Map lazily so it is not allocated on every render: `useRef<Map<...>>(null)`, filled on first use.

bugs.rootCause: Measured earlier on RF8Y60PP2XZ with atrace and framestats. I re-checked it against the library code: Reanimated 4.5.1 NodesManager.onEventDispatch, performNonLayoutOperations and getPendingUpdates; react-native-svg VirtualView.setClientRect; ReanimatedMountHook.handleNodeRemovals. react-native-svg sends a layout event for every shape the first time it draws it. On the UI thread, Reanimated answers every such event by re-applying the last props of every view it animated in the last 2 s. It does this whether or not any worklet listens: event to JSON, parse on the UI runtime, then a reflection call per view. A view deleted in that same frame is still in Reanimated's list until reportMount, which runs after the draw. Each re-apply then fails on it and logs an exception with a full stack trace, about 1 ms each. In the app the trigger was AvatarArt. Home's stage avatar turned into one still picture when Home was covered and back into layers on return, deleting freshly animated eye layers while 124–142 new shapes were drawn: 234–248 exceptions and 274/310 ms frames. The same happened at the end of every in-game avatar reaction, in the avatar picker and on avatar changes. HomeScreen also re-rendered its whole tree on every blur and focus. On top of that, each return to Home re-rendered it twice: practiceHistory.refresh set status 'loading' and then put in a new `recent` array even when nothing had changed. What remains comes from the library design and still needs native work. A new screen's first frame pays 'shapes drawn × views in Reanimated's list'. From the Reanimated code (not measured): any animated style that returns a `transform` array writes once on mount, because Reanimated compares arrays by reference. So the new screen's own tactile buttons, cards and Enter parts sit in that list for 2 s, which explains about 130 ms on 'משחק חדש'. There is also about 250–300 ms of JS (measured before the fixes), mostly react-native-svg building one React component per shape.
bugs.fix: Earlier round, kept: (1) AvatarArt: a covered stage keeps its layered stack and only stops its beats, so there is no swap to a still picture and back. (2) AvatarArt: stacks it no longer shows stay mounted, hidden (opacity 0, no plans), for LAYERS_RETIRE_MS = 4000 ms before they unmount. That is longer than Reanimated's 2–2.5 s window, so nothing it still holds is deleted while new SVG is drawn. The stack key includes the set of moving layers, and each stack sits in its own non-collapsable, ltr wrapper. (3) useScreenFocused(enabled) and HomeScreen useScreenFocused(entrance): after its entrance, Home does not render on blur or focus. This round: (4) New avatars/svgMarkup.tsx (SvgMarkup + svgAst). AvatarArt draws each SvgXml through it: react-native-svg's parse() result, with its elements built once, is kept in a 96-entry LRU keyed by the markup. It draws exactly what SvgXml drew, except that the markup string is no longer passed as a prop to the native Svg view. jest.setup.ts maps it to the same host element `SvgXml`, so every existing test reads the same thing. Gain measured in Jest: parse is about 7% of an avatar's JS (0.45 of 6.4 ms), so a few ms per avatar when a screen is opened again; a small gain, as the reviewer expected. (5) state/practiceHistory.ts, stale-while-revalidate: a list already read stays 'ready' while it is read again, and a read that finds the same games (compared row by row) changes nothing. So a return to Home no longer re-renders it twice. RecentGames already ignored 'loading' after the first read, so nothing on screen changes. (6) AvatarArt useRetiredStacks: the timers Map is created on first use and cleared on cleanup, so an effect re-run without an unmount restarts the timers (a hidden Activity shown again, Fast Refresh). (7) docs/PERF.md: B14 is marked partial in so many words. It records the exact native change that is still needed, the transform-array finding, the game→results check and the new tests. Not done, by decision: the Reanimated native patch in NodesManager.kt onEventDispatch (return early on the UI thread when isAnyHandlerWaitingForEvent is false, as the off-UI-thread branch already does). It needs a new dependency (patch-package plus a postinstall), a native build and a device check for flicker, scrolling and gestures. I may not install or build here, and it needs Moshe's OK. The proposed diff is at C:/Users/mosheg/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mosheg-Documents-ReactNative-sudoku-fight/4440d2fa-e446-41ad-83db-f79035cdf42c/scratchpad/perf/reanimated-onEventDispatch.patch. Expected gain: most of the ~130 ms first-draw frame on every new screen.

Reviewer issues:
- Medium (B14 not finished): addressed as far as low-risk JS allows.
  - Implemented the suggested parsed-SVG cache (SvgMarkup, a 96-entry LRU). I measured its value first: in Jest, parse is about 7% of an avatar's JS; the rest is react-native-svg building one component per shape.
  - Decided against the Reanimated native patch this round. It needs patch-package (a new dependency and postinstall, and an npm install in a working tree that ~10 agents share), a native build and its own device check, and the area rules forbid builds and require low-risk changes.
  - The exact diff is saved at C:/Users/mosheg/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mosheg-Documents-ReactNative-sudoku-fight/4440d2fa-e446-41ad-83db-f79035cdf42c/scratchpad/perf/reanimated-onEventDispatch.patch and described in PERF.md. It needs Moshe's OK.
  - Added framestats for 'שחק'→'משחק חדש', with pass criteria, to the deviceCheck.
- Low (homeTransitions hid the focus re-renders): fixed the cause rather than the wording. practiceHistory is now stale-while-revalidate, and the test runs the focus effect on every focus. Server-driven refreshes (refreshMyProgress, refreshMeIfStale) can still re-render Home when their data arrives, after the transition has started; PERF.md says so.
- Low (game→results): no code change, a deviceCheck step (f) instead, plus a note in PERF.md.
  - Reasoning: the results load asynchronously (load() returns a Promise; practice results come from SQLite), so their avatars most likely mount in a later frame than the one that deletes the game.
  - Stale tags there would also come from non-avatar game views (TimerRing, cells, Score), which AvatarArt cannot control.
  - ResultsScreen.tsx is being edited by another agent this workflow, so I did not touch it.
- Low (timers Map): fixed, with a regression test using React 19.2's Activity.

New finding, from the Reanimated 4.5.1 source and not measured: useAnimatedStyle seeds `last` with the initial style, and its first mapper run compares the `transform` arrays by reference. So every Animated.View with a transform style (each tactile button has 2, each PressableCard 1, each Enter 1) writes once on mount and stays in the props registry for 2 s. On a new screen, that list is mostly the screen's own buttons and cards, which is why the first draw of 278 shapes still costs about 130 ms.
- A JS-only alternative to the native patch: attach those animated styles only while moving, as Enter already does before it starts (B46).
- It touches press feedback app-wide, and tactile.tsx and Enter.tsx are being edited by other agents right now (slant, B46), so I left it as a documented follow-up.

Other decisions:
- AST_CACHE_SIZE = 96: a few dozen kB per tree, enough for a list screen plus the screens around it.
- SvgMarkup no longer hands the markup string to the native Svg view as a prop. SvgXml did, and the native view never used it.
- sameGames compares rows with JSON.stringify: 20 small plain rows from SQLite.

Shared files: jest.setup.ts got one small mock block next to the existing react-native-svg mock. AvatarArt.tsx keeps the B10 change (accessibilityValue only under NODE_ENV test). PERF.md edits stay inside the B14/B32 section.

bugs.rootCause: In apps/server/scripts/adb.ts, screen() ran 'uiautomator dump /sdcard/qa-ui.xml' and then catted the file without checking anything. On a screen that keeps animating, uiautomator's DumpCommand waits up to ~10s for idle. It then prints 'ERROR: could not get idle state.' to stderr, writes no file, and still exits 0. adb() looked only at stdout and the exit status, so the old dump from the previous screen was parsed and printed. 'tap "text"' uses the same screen(), so it could tap coordinates from a stale screen. 'shot' had a similar silent failure: 'adb exec-out' does not pass on the exit status and merges stderr into stdout. A failed screencap was written as a .png full of error text, and the path was printed as if it worked; with a fixed file name, nothing showed it was not a fresh picture. The other commands (tap x y, swipe, type, key, launch, stop, link, version, reset) read no file from the phone and already fail on a non-zero adb exit.
bugs.fix:
New pure helpers in apps/server/src/testing/qaAgent/index.ts:
- dumpUi(device, path) does, on each try: 'rm -f' the old dump, then 'uiautomator dump', then read the file back. It accepts only a whole hierarchy (isUiDump: <hierarchy …</hierarchy> at the end). It makes UI_DUMP_TRIES=3 tries, UI_DUMP_RETRY_MS=500 apart, then throws 'uiautomator could not read the screen (3 tries): <uiautomator's own message>'. When the message is the idle-state error, it adds a hint.
- isPng(data) checks the 8-byte PNG header.

In adb.ts:
- adb() is split into run() (keeps stderr) and adb().
- A 'phone' UiDumpDevice passes stdout+stderr for shell calls and uses Atomics.wait for the sync sleep.
- screen() now uses dumpUi, so 'ui' and 'tap "…"' exit 1 with the reason and never print or tap old data.
- 'shot' deletes the target file first and checks the PNG header; on failure it throws 'screencap gave no picture: …' (exit 1) and leaves no file under that name.
- The header usage text describes the new behaviour.

  (c) 'shot' deletes the given file name before capturing, so a failure never leaves an older picture under that name.

The header is 329px tall at 360px width (6 rows) and 425px at 320px (8 rows). At 180px width, which is what 200% page zoom gives on a 360px phone, it is 761px (15 rows). Nothing overflows sideways at any of these widths.
issues.suggestion: Can wait for a later polish pass. Options: put the language list in a <details> menu (no script needed, safe under the CSP), use smaller padding or font for the links, or keep it as is. Worth stating in the Hebrew report as a known look change.

issues.problem: The Q2 retry and its clear message depend on how adb behaves, and that was never checked on a phone: `adb exec-out` should exit 0 and pass stderr through as stdout, while `uiautomator dump` should exit 0 and print its error to stderr. If uiautomator or `exec-out cat` ever exits non-zero, run() throws at once (adb.ts:68-69). There is then no retry and no hint, and the message is something like 'adb exec-out cat /sdcard/qa-ui.xml: exit 1'. This still never returns stale data, so the bug itself stays fixed. The header also says 'up to ~30 s', but 3 tries at about 10s of idle wait each, plus uiautomator's start-up time and 2×500ms sleeps, come to roughly 33–37s.
issues.evidence: The device with rm/uiautomator/read is faked in qaAgent.test.ts, and only the pure dumpUi/isUiDump/isPng helpers are tested. The `phone` adapter (adb.ts:85-92) and the shot path (adb.ts:143-156) have no automated test. The fixer says RF8Y80NPLZW was not connected, and `adb devices -l` still lists only RF8Y30L038L and RF8Y60PP2XZ, so I could not run a live dump either. AOSP DumpCommand and the adb exec: service do behave as the fixer describes, so the logic is very likely right.
issues.suggestion: Run the fixer's device check (steps 1–5) once RF8Y80NPLZW is connected, especially 'ui' on Home with the floating digits, and 'ls /sdcard/qa-ui.xml' after a failed run. Optionally change the header to say 'about 35 s'.
